context: A police officer briefs a uni reporter about a retail-safety case
purpose: Teach: 通路/通話/品種/実体/原点/ネーム/努める/写し

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 商業施設の通路、保安上の議論、よく話題に上ります。
lines.en: Mall corridors come up a lot in security discussions.
lines.style: Even, informative tone. Measured pace. Slight professional distance. Opening phrase lands with quiet certainty — this is settled ground.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 品種別の通話確認、行うこともあるんですか。
lines.en: Do you ever conduct verification calls for different types of incidents?
lines.style: Thoughtful, respectful inquiry. Slight hesitation before the question — he's genuinely uncertain about protocol, not testing. Lean forward slightly in posture.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: はい。実体ある現場検証も、原点に立つ仕事です。
lines.en: Yes. Actual fieldwork verification is where the fundamentals matter most.
lines.style: Firm, grounded tone. Quiet conviction on 'fundamentals' — he's drawing on experience. Not lecturing, just stating what he knows. Steady eye contact.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 通報ネーム、警察側で記録されてるんでしょうか。
lines.en: Are reporter names kept on record by the police?
lines.style: Tentative but direct. Slight lift at the end — genuine question, not accusatory. Careful about phrasing; he's navigating sensitive territory thoughtfully.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 匿名性の確保に努める方針ですが、写しの管理は厳重です。
lines.en: We make every effort to protect anonymity, but we maintain strict control over any records.
lines.style: Professional, reassuring cadence. Slight warmth beneath the formality — he understands why this matters. Measured, declarative delivery. No defensiveness.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。
lines.style: Quiet, genuine. Slight bow forward in voice — real appreciation, not perfunctory. Brief exhale after, settling the conversation.
